ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), as amended, implemented through the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Obligations of Reporting Entities) Regulations 2011; sanctions administered under the United Nations Sanctions Act 2020, the Russia Sanctions Act 2022, and the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002; corporate UBO transparency governed by the Companies Act 1993, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 2021, and the Companies (Disclosure of Ultimate Ownership and Control) Regulations 2023, which require every New Zealand company to maintain an internal Particulars of Ownership and Control (POC) register; registered office and name provisions governed by the Companies Act 1993, sections 20-26 and 207-209.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - the shareholder and director registers are fully public on the New Zealand Companies Register, but the statutorily mandated UBO/Particulars of Ownership and Control (POC) register is non-public and is accessible only to the Registrar, AML/CFT supervisors, and law enforcement agencies on lawful demand; nominee or trustee arrangements are legally permissible only if the POC register truthfully discloses the ultimate natural-person controllers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 5, 10-16, 40-47, 57-58, 85-92, 122, 151-152 and 159; New Zealand Business Number Act 2016; Financial Reporting Act 2013; Income Tax Act 2007; Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017 for licensing interface purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating through the Companies Register and the Companies Online electronic filing platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (statutory electronic application submitted via Companies Online), culminating in the Registrar's Certificate of Incorporation and automatic issuance of the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies under the Companies Act 1993; the Company may be incorporated with one or more shares of nil par value or nominal par value (customarily NZD 0.01 to NZD 1.00 per share). No escrow account is required for formation purposes; the subscriber must pay only the consideration fixed by board resolution, and the share register must record the allotment in accordance with sections 40 and 85-92 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [FULL COMPANY NAME] LTD (the Company), ADOPTED AS WRITTEN RESOLUTIONS PURSUANT TO SECTION 122 AND SECTIONS 151-152 OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993 (NEW ZEALAND) ON [DATE]. WHEREAS: (A) the Company was incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 under Company Number [NZCN/XXXX] and New Zealand Business Number [NZBN/XXXXXXXX]; (B) the Company Constitution permits the board to issue shares, fix the registered office and appoint officers; (C) the subscriber has applied to take shares. IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: that the subscription application of [Subscriber Full Name] for 1,000 fully paid ordinary shares (no par value) at an issue price of NZD 0.10 per share (total subscription consideration NZD 100.00) be and the same is hereby approved, that the said shares be allotted to the subscriber effective the date of this resolution, that the subscriber's name be entered in the share register pursuant to sections 85-92 of the Companies Act 1993, and that share certificates be signed and issued in accordance with the Constitution. 2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE: that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at [Registered Office Street Address, City, Postcode], New Zealand pursuant to section 57 of the Companies Act 1993, that this address serve as the Company's address for service, and that any change be notified to the Registrar in accordance with section 58. 3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: that [Full Name], a New Zealand resident, be and is hereby appointed Director and Chairperson with effect immediately, having delivered a signed consent to act in accordance with section 152(1); that [Full Name] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary and Chief Financial Officer with authority to file statutory returns with the Companies Office, Inland Revenue and the NZBN Registrar; and that [Full Name] be and is hereby appointed Health and Safety and Hazardous Substances Compliance Officer for the battery testing laboratory under the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017. 4. BANKING AND GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: that the Director and the Secretary, jointly and severally, be and are hereby authorized to open corporate bank accounts, to operate target payment rails (wire transfer and Wise), and to execute and file all incorporation, licensing and registration documents on behalf of the Company. 5. COMMENCEMENT OF OPERATIONAL LICENSING: that the officers be and are hereby directed to advance the ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for UN38.3 T1-T6 battery drop testing and CE-RED electromagnetic compatibility testing (ISIC 7120 / NAICS 541380), the environmental impact assessment registration, the hazardous substances location authorization, the fire safety clearance, and the civil defense and building warrant approvals. DULY PASSED this [Day] day of [Month], [Year], at [City], New Zealand. Signed: Director and Chairperson; Company Secretary and Chief Financial Officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search and NZBN Availability Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO) - Companies Register online portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a formal name availability search on the Companies Register to confirm the proposed corporate name (e.g., [NAME] BATTERY SAFETY TESTING LIMITED) is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Verify whether the proposed name contains a restricted or offensive expression under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993 and obtain written consent from any named individual if the name includes a personal name. Commence the Companies Online application shell and record the reserved name and NZBN entity details entered by the applicant.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name availability search report (Companies Register printout)
Written consent for the use of an individual's name in the company name (if applicable)
Certified copy of the incorporating applicant's passport or national identity document
Customer due diligence (CDD) and know-your-client (KYC) statement of the intended subscriber and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for similarity or restricted words, submit an amended name through the same Companies Online application shell and re-run the availability search; where the refusal is based on an offensive word, file a written reconsideration request with the Companies Office and await the Registrar's written determination before re-lodging.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitution and Subscriber Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand incorporation agent and registered legal counsel acting for the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Company Constitution pursuant to section 15 of the Companies Act 1993, prescribing the board composition (minimum one director), share class rights, director indemnities, quorum rules and any entrenchment provisions. Prepare the subscriber application for shares, the consent-to-act forms for each proposed director under section 152(1), and the initial share register template. Verify that the constitutional details are fully consistent with the data that will be keyed into the Companies Online incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Constitution of the Company (adopted and executed for registration)
Signed subscriber application for shares
Statutory declarations and identity/CIP records for directors and beneficial owners
Notices of intended director appointment and signed consents to act (section 152)
Initial share register and share certificate templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the constitution or consent forms are defective, amend and re-execute the relevant instruments with fresh signatures; if a proposed director is disqualified under section 383 of the Companies Act 1993, substitute a qualified director and issue a replacement consent before proceeding to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Application with the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO) - Companies Online / NZBN corporate registration portal operated by MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to Companies Online using a verified RealMe account or the authorized incorporation agent's intermediary service. Complete the statutory Application for Registration of a Company by entering the company name, company type (company limited by shares), the physical registered office address (a New Zealand street address, not a post office box), the address for service, the applicant's details, the full names, residential addresses and dates of birth of all current and intended directors, and the names and shareholding details of the subscriber; select optional registration of the constitution; tick the election for the automatic issue of the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Pay the Companies Office incorporation fee (NZD 127.64 inclusive of GST, approximately USD 80) online by credit card or POLi. Submit the application and retain the electronic acknowledgement and case number. Upon validation, the Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and the NZBN.
required_dossiers: Completed online Application for Registration of a Company (Companies Online form)
Statutory consent-to-act forms for each director (section 152)
Company Constitution (where registration of the constitution is elected)
Registered office and address for service particulars
Proof of payment of the Companies Office incorporation fee (NZD 127.64 / approximately USD 80)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application (e.g., invalid registered office address, incomplete consent forms, or suspended name), the agent must respond through Companies Online correspondence within five working days, correct the deficient fields and re-submit; if the application is rejected, pay the applicable re-lodgement fee and file a fresh application; if a direction is refused for disqualification, substitute a qualified director before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Capital Subscription, Allotment and Establishment of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company and the corporate secretarial service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive the share subscription consideration (NZD 100.00 or the amount fixed by board resolution) into the Company's bank account or the incorporation agent's client trust account. Record the receipt, execute the first board resolution, allot the 1,000 ordinary shares, enter the allotment in the share register, and issue the share certificates. Prepare the statutory registers (register of shares, register of directors, register of charges if any) and the minutes of the first board meeting, and file the annual return establishment records with the Companies Office.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of the share subscription consideration (bank transfer or trust account receipt)
Share certificates issued to the subscriber
Share allotment journal and share register entries
Minutes of the First Board of Directors Meeting
Directors' and secretarial appointment records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any share register entry error by a correcting board resolution; if the bank account opening is delayed, retain the subscription receipt issued by the licensed trust account and record it in the minutes; re-execute any defective board minutes with unanimous director signature before statutory reliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Tax Registration and NZBN Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue (IRD), New Zealand - myIR online business registration portal; NZBN Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online through Inland Revenue's myIR portal to register the Company for New Zealand income tax (company tax rate 28%), goods and services tax (GST) at the standard 15% rate (mandatory if taxable turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 per annum, optional below that threshold), and PAYE employer registration if test laboratory staff are to be engaged. Complete the IR596 company registration form or the equivalent online new business registration workflow, submit the certificate of incorporation, and verify that the NZBN record automatically created by the Companies Office is activated with the appropriate industrial classification code (ISIC 7120 technical testing and analysis; NAICS 541380; ANZSIC 6712).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Company constitution extract and share register extract
Directors' and ultimate beneficial owners' IRD numbers (to the extent required by IRD rules)
Business industry classification details (ISIC 7120; NAICS 541380; ANZSIC 6712)
Directors' personal tax information forms (IR596 related schedules)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD registration is not completed within the standard service window, escalate through the myIR secure correspondence channel and request a priority allocation; correct any mismatched director IRD numbers; if the GST registration is issued for the wrong class of activity, lodge a formal correction request with Inland Revenue before the first taxable period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Physical and Environmental Licensing Initiation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: International Accreditation New Zealand (IANZ); WorkSafe New Zealand; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); the Territorial Authority/Building Consent Authority; the Regional Council as Resource Management Act consent authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN, file the ISO/IEC 17025 testing laboratory accreditation application with IANZ covering the UN38.3 T1-T6 battery drop, impact, thermal, vibration, short-circuit and crush test methods and the CE-RED electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) test methods. Submit the hazardous substances location application (Class 9 dangerous goods - lithium cells) to WorkSafe New Zealand. Lodge the short-form assessment of environmental effects (AEE) and discharge/waste authorizations with the relevant Regional Council and, where applicable, the Environmental Protection Authority. Submit the building consent and code-compliance application to the Territorial Authority for the drop-test cell and EMC screened room, and file the fire safety evacuation scheme with Fire and Emergency New Zealand. Procure the electrical safety certificate under AS/NZS 3000 from a licensed electrical inspector.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN certificate
Laboratory site lease or title evidence for the New Zealand test facility
ISO/IEC 17025 quality manual and test procedures for UN38.3 T1-T6 and CE-RED EMC testing
Hazardous substances location application (Class 9) to WorkSafe New Zealand
Environmental assessment of environmental effects (short-form AEE) and waste management plan
Fire safety and evacuation scheme application to Fire and Emergency New Zealand
Electrical safety compliance certificate for test apparatus (AS/NZS 3000)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IANZ accreditation application is queried, respond to the technical review comments within the prescribed 20 working days and submit the revised quality manual; if the land-use or discharge consent is declined, lodge an amended application or appeal to the Environment Court where the decision is reviewable; if the hazardous substances location certificate is rejected, correct the fire-rated storage layout and re-submit to WorkSafe; if the fire safety evacuation scheme is declined, amend the fire safety plan and re-file the revised certificate through FENZ.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: International Accreditation New Zealand (IANZ) as the national accreditation body for testing laboratories; WorkSafe New Zealand for hazardous substances location licensing; and the Territorial Authority / Building Consent Authority for structural and physical clearance of the test facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Testing Laboratory Accreditation Certificate (test scope: UN38.3 T1-T6 drop, impact, thermal, vibration, short-circuit and crush testing of lithium cells and batteries, together with CE-RED electromagnetic compatibility testing under EN 55011 and EN 61000-4-3); Hazardous Substances Location Licence (Class 9 dangerous goods) issued by WorkSafe New Zealand; and Building Consent occupancy approval for the physical test bay.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) at the national policy level, acting in coordination with the relevant Regional Council as the consent authority under the Resource Management Act 1991 (site-specific authority: Auckland Council / Waikato Regional Council as applicable).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Registration (Controlled/Permitted Activity) with a short-form Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE); a full EIA Report under Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991 is not required given the small-scale, enclosed nature of the laboratory, the limited handling of Class 9 battery substances, and the absence of significant off-site discharges; site-specific discharge permits and hazardous waste authorizations are nevertheless required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Disharge and emissions compliance thresholds are as follows: (a) sanitary wastewater and cooling water discharge at the facility boundary requires pH in the range 6.5-8.5 and heavy metal maxima of cadmium not exceeding 0.05 mg/L, lead not exceeding 0.10 mg/L, nickel not exceeding 0.20 mg/L and cobalt not exceeding 0.20 mg/L, with zero discharge of battery electrolyte solvents to stormwater systems; (b) airborne thermal-test vent emissions shall not exceed a total volatile organic compound (VOC) concentration of 1.0 mg/m³ at the facility boundary, with electromagnetic emissions limited to EN 55011 Class A levels measured at 30 metres; (c) spent lithium battery waste (UN3480 and UN3481) must be classified as Class 9 dangerous goods, stored in a fire-rated container with a maximum quantity of 5,000 kg per location, and consigned through a licensed hazardous waste transporter to a permitted disposal facility in accordance with the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017 and applicable EPA waste guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate and Fire Evacuation Scheme approval issued by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) or Certificate of Acceptance issued under the Building Act 2004 confirming the structural load rating (minimum 10 kN) of the drop-test mass, the reinforced concrete slab, and the EMC screened room; occupational health and safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including the appointment of a Person in Control of the hazardous substances location, a documented lithium battery thermal-runaway fire-response plan, and the electrical safety certificate issued under AS/NZS 3000 for all energized test apparatus; all test operators must hold current competency and hazard-response training records prior to commencement of UN38.3 testing operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tāke) — myIR portal at ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity deriving New Zealand-source income or carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand must first obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) through the Companies Office and then apply to Inland Revenue for a tax file number (IRD number). Non-resident companies use form IR596, while resident or carrying-on-business companies use form IR595; applications can be submitted electronically through myIR or by a registered tax agent. The application must include certificate of incorporation, registered office details, director information and, for non-resident applicants, evidence of the New Zealand tax agent or local address for service. Once the IRD number is assigned, the entity must file GST and income tax returns if turnover exceeds relevant thresholds or if NZ-source income is derived; a foreign entity with no NZ taxable presence is generally not required to register for an IRD number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box election system. Eligible close companies may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status under subpart HA of the Income Tax Act 2007 to pass through tax attributes to shareholders. Certain foreign-owned companies may elect to be treated as non-resident or as exempt from tax on non-New Zealand-sourced income, and cross-border hybrid mismatch elections may be required or available under the OECD-aligned BEPS rules. No general tax-haven exemption is available; any specific statutory exemption must be claimed by filing the appropriate IRD return or election form.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API invoice authorisation. E-invoicing via the PEPPOL network is voluntary. Suppliers must issue tax invoices that satisfy section 24 of the GST Act, including supplier name, GST number, invoice date, description of supply, and GST amount. The Inland Revenue may request electronic records during audit; no pre-clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods is zero-rated as an export if the supplier exports the goods within 28 days of the time of supply to a destination outside New Zealand and retains documentary evidence prescribed by section 11 of the GST Act. Services performed directly in connection with goods intended for export may also be zero-rated if provided to a non-resident outside New Zealand, provided the services are not supplied to a person in New Zealand and not for use in New Zealand. Technical testing and analysis services for exported battery goods may qualify, subject to the supplier holding sufficient evidence of destination, export, and payment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (CusDec) through New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export
Commercial invoice and contract of supply
Inward remittance certificate or bank payment proof confirming foreign currency repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits export zero-rating claimants with particular attention to physical export timing, documentary evidence, and currency remittance. If goods are not exported within 28 days, or if documentation is insufficient, GST of 15% becomes payable and use-of-money interest runs from the original time of supply. Fraudulent or abusive export claims attract shortfall penalties of 20%, 40%, or 100% of the tax shortfall, plus criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act. The Commissioner may also claw back refunds previously issued and require repayment of any GST input credits claimed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible for residents and non-residents without exchange-control approval. Profit remittances, dividends, interest, loan repayments, royalty payments, and capital repatriation are not subject to central bank licensing or administrative conversion limits. The only relevant filter is banking-channel due diligence, Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 compliance, taxation at source for certain outbound payments, and the Overseas Investment Act 2005 regime for acquisitions of sensitive land, significant business assets, or fishing quotas. No government approval is required for an International Company incorporated under a permitted foreign statute to open a treasury account in New Zealand or to inject equity capital from a non-resident parent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement. There is no mandated timeline for converting foreign-currency export receipts into NZD and no mandatory conversion ratio. The default ratio is 0%, meaning an exporter may retain 100% of export receipts in an acceptable foreign-currency account or convert them to NZD according to commercial treasury policy and the exporter's banking relationship.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary payment collection and Multi-Currency treasury routing, but Low for acting as the principal corporate banking, escrow, or trade-finance account provider. Wise New Zealand Limited is not a registered bank under the Prudential Supervision of Banks in New Zealand framework; it operates as a financial service provider and payment intermediary. It may hold funds for payment transmission incidental to cross-border trading, but it cannot provide regulated banking products such as commercial letters of credit, banker's acceptances, or RTGS settlement. Offshore digital EMIs must comply with the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 if they provide services into New Zealand. Corporate treasury should use a licensed domestic bank as the primary account and use fintech rails solely for expedited low-value settlement or employee expense disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand law does not mandate a physical in-branch KYC interview for non-resident corporate clients. Banks apply risk-based procedures and generally permit remote onboarding with video-verified directors, certified passport copies, and independent electronic identity checks. In practice, an offshore tax-exempt International Company with non-resident beneficial owners will usually require at least one video-conference interview with the designated compliance officer, and some banks require a natural-person director or a New Zealand-resident authorised signatory. Physical appearance at a branch is not a statutory condition, but the ultimate beneficial owners, source of funds, commercial purpose, and business premises of the battery-safety testing laboratory must be documented to a standard that allows the bank to complete enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The applicant is a tax-exempt International Company with no visible economic substance in New Zealand and a structure that appears designed to benefit from zero taxation while operating a laboratory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing from the registering jurisdiction; certified Memorandum of Association and Articles; register of directors and shareholders; group organogram; signed statement of economic activity in New Zealand; lease or service agreement for the battery testing laboratory; New Zealand shareholder and employee details; projected financial statements; and an explanatory board memorandum describing the UN 38.3 and CE-RED testing business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital contribution from a non-resident parent or offshore trust aimed at funding the laboratory is flagged as unusual and inconsistent with the projected operational size.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed capital injection board resolution; facility and equipment purchase contracts; ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation scope or application; audited or management financial statements; bank reference from the remitting institution; source-of-wealth statement from the contributing beneficial owner; tax clearance certificates or equivalent; and traceable chain-of-funds evidence from the parent account to the New Zealand treasury account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The declared industry classification of dangerous-goods testing creates ambiguity because the bank is unable to determine whether the company trades in physical battery inventory or performs only laboratory services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal representation on the ISIC 7120 and NAICS 541380 classification; detailed scope of testing work; sample UN38.3 test plan; contracts with battery manufacturers; certificates of accreditation for fixture and environmental testing; WorkSafe New Zealand hazardous-substance notifications where applicable; and a clear statement that the entity does not sell batteries itself but provides compliance certification for third-party products.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or export-control exposure is suspected because battery testing hardware, calibration equipment, or CE-RED documentation services may be associated with military or controlled end-users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user and end-use declarations from all major customers; UN number and dangerous-goods class list; export control classification list for test equipment; denied-party screening results; supplier and customer sanction-screen logs; compliance policy manual; and customs broker documentation identifying all physical movements of calibration instruments and reference batteries.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inward treasury payments should be effected through the SWIFT network using MT103 for direct client-to-beneficiary transfer or MT202 for bank-to-bank interbank cover. The originating bank must include a clear narrative purpose in Field 72 or Field 77B, with a description such as 'Equity capital contribution for battery safety testing laboratory operations'. Where the correspondent bank asks for a category purpose code, one should use the SWIFT Category Purpose Code 'EQUI' for equity investment, 'CINV' for capital investment, or the bank's agreed Open-Banking statistical code for services. The receiving New Zealand bank must perform sanctions screening, source-of-funds verification, and beneficial-owner confirmation before crediting the account. Any capital contribution to an International Company must be reconciled with the company's issued-share records, board minutes, and the New Zealand branch's internal funding ledger. If the international company has no New Zealand registration, the bank may require a local address, a recognised authorised representative, and tax information collection under the CRS framework.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade payments from the New Zealand treasury account should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct settlement of supplier invoices and service fees, and via commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 rules for significant capital equipment or recurring battery-component purchases. The letter-of-credit channel is expected to use MT700 for issuance, MT707 for amendments, and MT202 for cover payments after compliant presentation. For NZD-denominated domestic clearing, the bank routes payments through the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) for real-time settlement. Correspondent banks in USD, EUR, or GBP should be pre-approved by the New Zealand relationship manager, and all outbound disbursement instructions must specify the beneficiary's full legal name, account number, BIC, purpose, commercial invoice reference, and Incoterms basis to avoid AML exception queues.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards once the underlying commercial exposure is documented
European and American FX options purchased for mandatory protection against adverse rate movement
Cross-currency swaps for long-term treasury matching and balance-sheet hedging
Commercially justified non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the counterparty is an authorised bank branch outside New Zealand
Exchange-traded FX futures cleared through recognised futures exchanges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's annual return date, which is the last day of the financial year (balance date); the Companies Office issues an electronic reminder to the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an offence under section 211 of the Companies Act 1993, with a fine up to NZ$10,000. The Registrar may issue a notice of intention to remove the company, and if the return remains unfiled after 20 working days, the company is struck off the Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Filing (with auditor's report when applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Financial Reporting Section, Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For large or overseas companies: the board must sign the financial statements within 4 months after balance date and deliver them to the Companies Office within 5 working days after signing. Small owner-managed companies are exempt from filing unless shareholders holding 5% or more require an audit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-lodgment is an offence punishable by a fine up to NZ$10,000 for the company and its directors; persistent default may trigger director disqualification and removal of the company from the Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: International Accreditation New Zealand (IANZ), the national testing laboratory accreditation body
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual on-site surveillance within 12 months of initial grant; full reassessment every 4 years; accreditation remains conditional on continuing compliance with ISO/IEC 17025 and UN38.3 test methods.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-conformance findings may lead to suspension or withdrawal of accreditation, rendering UN38.3 battery safety test reports invalid for export and regulatory certification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is mandatory for a 'large' New Zealand company meeting any two of three thresholds: total assets at or above NZ$60 million, revenue at or above NZ$30 million, or 100 or more employees. Audit is also mandatory for FMC reporting entities under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 and for overseas companies required to file financial statements in New Zealand. Shareholders holding 5% or more of voting shares may compel an audit under section 200 of the Companies Act 1993. The UN38.3 battery safety testing laboratory is expected to be small or owner-managed and therefore exempt from compulsory audit absent a shareholder request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (Tier 1); NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2) for non-large entities; NZ Simple Format Reporting Standard (Tier 3) for small entities. All financial statements must comply with the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies Act 1993 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009: (1) any share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members before the next annual return; (2) the annual return confirms current shareholders and directors with the Companies Office, and New Zealand does not currently operate a public beneficial-ownership filing; (3) for AML/CFT-reporting entities, beneficial ownership must be re-verified on trigger events and on a risk-based review cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholder and director meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$250-US$1,200 per year (NZD 400-NZD 2,000) for a New Zealand registered office and corporate agent service.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000-US$18,000 for a small or owner-managed battery safety testing laboratory with UN38.3 and CE-RED scope; fees vary with transaction complexity and the applicable Tier 2 reporting framework.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays under New Zealand domestic law. The effective tax rate may be reduced by: (i) the 15% Research and Development (R&D) tax credit (Income Tax Act 2007, s LA 5); (ii) unlimited carry-forward of tax losses subject to 49% shareholder continuity; (iii) depreciation deductions, including straight-line or diminishing value; and (iv) Approved Issuer Levy at 2% on qualifying interest if the company elects this treatment. There is no targeted reduction for a non-resident-controlled company.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite, subject to 49% shareholder continuity requirement)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - Company Income Tax Return filed electronically through the Inland Revenue Department's myIR portal (or via a tax agent's approved electronic filing software).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 return for a standard 31 March balance date is due by 7 July immediately following the end of the income year. Where the company uses a tax agent with a current extension schedule, the deadline is generally extended to 31 March of the following income year. Terminal tax payment is due on the 7th of the month following the balance date (typically 7 May for a March balance date) unless on a tax agent extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, IRD number (tax file number), balance date, registered address, and principal business activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must quote their New Zealand IRD registration number and the branch (NBR) number. The principal business code should reflect ISIC 7120 (technical testing and analysis).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross income from testing services, laboratory fees, government grants, interest, dividends, and other assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only New Zealand-sourced income unless a lesser amount is assessable under the relevant double tax agreement (DTA). Foreign income derived by a non-resident company is generally not assessable in NZ.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs, rent, salaries, consumables, depreciation of testing equipment, subcontractor fees, insurance, and other expenses incurred in deriving assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses connected with and directly attributable to New Zealand-source income are deductible. Overhead apportionment must be reasonable and documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjusting for non-deductible items such as entertainment expenses (50% disallowance) and fines or penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the net result is a loss, the non-resident company must still file the IR4 to record the loss in its NZ tax account. The loss can be carried forward subject to continuity provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year tax losses applied against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss offset is permitted only if the company maintains at least 49% continuity of shareholder identity and the loss belonged to the same company. A non-resident company with a NZ branch cannot utilise foreign losses against NZ-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Closing debit/credit balance of the company's imputation account for New Zealand tax on distributed profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder may receive imputation credits only if the company is New Zealand-resident. Non-resident withholding tax is generally charged on dividends gross of imputation credits unless reduced by a DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax due after payment of provisional tax, R&D credits, and other credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The terminal tax must be paid by the statutory due date. Late payment triggers use-of-money interest and late payment penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: immediate NZ$250, plus NZ$250 for each further month or part month the return remains outstanding thereafter, capped at NZ$4,000. Late payment penalties apply on the unpaid tax: 1% on the first day of default, 4% on the 7th day, and a further 1% per month thereafter (maximum additional 8% in total). For repeated or evasion-related failures, shortfall penalties can escalate to 150% of the tax shortfall.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (non-resident withholding tax), reduced under applicable DTA treaty rates (commonly 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% for shareholdings of 10% or more in the paying company).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must provide the New Zealand payer with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of its country of residence before the dividend payment. The payer must retain this certificate on file and apply the reduced treaty withholding rate at source. If the certificate cannot be obtained before payment, the payer must withhold at the 30% domestic rate, and the non-resident may claim a refund from Inland Revenue by filing a New Zealand income tax return (IR4/IR3) and attaching the TRC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 15% NRWT (statutory) or 2% Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) if the lending is non-associated and meets the conditions; royalties: 15% NRWT (statutory). DTA treaty rates frequently reduce interest to 10% and royalties to 5%-10%, depending on the treaty and the IP character.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 1,000,000 (aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions in an income year). This triggers the requirement to prepare and contemporaneously retain transfer pricing documentation (Local File + Master File equivalent) supporting the arm's length character of the transactings.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime as seen in BVI/Cayman. However, the Income Tax Act 2007 requires genuine economic substance for a company to be treated as a New Zealand tax resident and to give effect to deductions. The GAAR (s BG 1) and the transfer pricing, CFC, and thin-capitalisation rules effectively require real local activity. A New Zealand company that is part of a tax-exempt offshore International Company structure with no employees, premises, or decision-making in New Zealand will be vulnerable to being re-characterised as an agent or conduit, and its income reallocated to the principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Concealment of Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately not filing the IR4, suppressing income from battery safety testing, artificially creating inflated deductible costs, or diverting revenue to a tax-exempt International Company while claiming a loss in New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal liability under Part 4 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 (s 143B): upon conviction, an individual is liable to a fine not exceeding NZ$1,000,000 and/or imprisonment not exceeding 5 years; a body corporate is liable to a fine not exceeding NZ$1,000,000. In addition, a shortfall penalty for evasion of up to 150% of the tax shortfall may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in the evasion are personally liable for the criminal fine; they may also be ordered by the court to pay restitution of the unpaid tax. Inland Revenue may issue a border stop order (travel ban) for tax debts exceeding NZ$25,000 and directors may be barred from leaving New Zealand. Imprisonment up to 5 years can be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham / Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a 'brass plate' New Zealand company that issues UN38.3/CE-RED test reports without actual fixed assets or qualified personnel, while the substantial profit is channelled to a tax-exempt 'International Company' (e.g., Cook Islands International Company) controlled by the same shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner of Inland Revenue may invoke s BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 to disregard the intervening entity or reallocate income to the New Zealand company. Transfer pricing adjustments and disallowed deductions can result in a tax shortfall, on which shortfall penalties of 20% (unacceptable tax position), 100% (abusive tax position), or 150% (evasion) may be applied. The company may also be struck off under the Companies Act 1993.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable under s 300 of the Companies Act 1993 for reckless trading if the company continues to operate while insolvent after the Commissioner's assessment. Courts may order civil compensation and disqualify the individual from managing companies for up to 10 years. A travel ban may be imposed for unpaid assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management fees, royalties, or interest to a related tax-exempt International Company without documenting the arm's length nature, causing New Zealand taxable income to be materially understated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue re-determines the arm's length price under subpart GC and may impose a transfer pricing adjustment. The resulting tax shortfall attracts shortfall penalties (20% for unacceptable tax position; 100% for abusive tax position) plus use-of-money interest from the date the tax would have been payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the defective tax return are exposed to personal liability under the Tax Administration Act 1994 as 'wholly or partly responsible' for the shortfall penalty, provided they knew of the tax position. The penalties attach directly to the director's personal assets; travel bans can be issued for unpaid penalties exceeding NZ$25,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) / Countering Financing of Terrorism (CFT) Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using multiple wire-payment rail accounts (including Wise) without conducting customer due diligence, or using the International Company as a pass-through conduit to obscure the origin of testing fees that are in fact criminal proceeds from fraudulent certification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, a reporting entity that breaches CDD, record-keeping, or suspicious activity reporting obligations is liable to a civil penalty up to NZ$2 million for a body corporate and NZ$50,000 for an individual. Where the conduct amounts to money laundering under the Crimes Act 1961 (s 243), an individual is liable to imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine up to NZ$2,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted as a principal party if they directed or facilitated the laundering. In addition to imprisonment, the High Court may make an assets forfeiture order under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009. Directors may also be disqualified and their passports cancelled; a travel ban is available against them as a condition of bail.
